To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the concentrations of PCDD/Fs and dioxin-like and non-dioxine-like PCBs in blood of pregnant women were 3-23, 3-20, and 16-326 pg TEQ/g lipid and 12-253 ng/g lipid, respectively.
the concentrations of PCDD/F, dioxin like PCB, and non dioxin-like-PCB in the breast milk of the Japanese women are low compared to those in the breast milk from the other countries.
the levels of PCDDs and PCDFs in breast milk were higher than those in blood, whereas those of PCBs in breast milk and blood were almost equal.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the concentrations of PCDD/Fs, dioxins-like PCBs, non-dioxin like PCBs in maternal blood and breast milk in Japan, which is the first study to report the concentrations of these compounds in the blood and breast milk from the same mothers.
the concentrations and partitioning ratios of PCDDs/PCDFs and PCBs in the blood and breast milk from pregnant women in Hokkaido, Japan.

the partitioning of dioxin-like and non-dioxins-like PCBs in the maternal blood to breast-milk in Japanese women, and the results will be useful in the assessment of the exposure of infants to dioxins and PCBs via lactation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the partitioning of PCDDs/PCDFs and PCB congeners from maternal blood to milk in women is affected by delivery, and that the partition of PCBs with chlorine at the specific positions of the biphenylic ring from the maternal blood to the breast-milk is more likely to occur than that of the other congeners.
the levels of PCDDs and PCDFs, and non-ortho and mono-ortho dioxin-like and non-dioxins-like PCBs in breast milk of Japanese women are relatively low compared with those in other countries.
the partition of PCBs and dioxins from blood to breastmilk in women is little influenced by pregnancy and delivery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the levels of PCDDs and PCDFs in the breast milk of primiparous and the secundiparous women were higher than the corresponding levels in the blood, whereas the levels of PCBs in the blood were higher than those in breast milk.

the partitioning of PCDDs/PCDFs and dioxin-like/non-dioxin-like-PCBs from maternal blood to the breast-milk of Japanese primiparous and/or secundiparous women is little affected, and that the partitioning levels of congeners with chlorine atoms at the 2, 3, 4' or 5-positions in the biphenyl rings from maternal blood to human breast milk are slightly higher than those of congeners with other chlorine

the levels of PCDDs and PCDFs in the breast milk of the Japanese mothers are lower than those in the breast milk collected from the European mothers, but the levels of non-dioxin like-PCBs in the breast milk are similar to or slightly higher than those of the European mothers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the partition ratios of PCDDs/PCDFs, dixoin-like PCBs, non-dioxinlike PCBs from maternal blood to the breastmilk are almost the same between primiparous and multiparous women.
the partitioning of dioxin-like and non-dioxins like PCBs from maternal blood to the breastmilk in women is not affected by delivery.
we were able to show that the levels of PCDDs and PCDFs in the breast milk of primiparous and secondiparous mothers were similar.
